public_rationale: Marcus's seven March 2024 predictions were: 7-10 GPT-4 level models, no massive advance, price wars, very little moat, no robust fix for hallucinations, modest corporate adoption, and modest profits split 7-10 ways. Several held by December 2024. ByteDance, Alibaba and Baidu cut model prices steeply in a reported price war. OpenAI itself called hallucinations an open problem in October 2024, and no GPT-5 had been released. But the leading developer, OpenAI, expected about a $5 billion loss in 2024 rather than modest profits. Also, OpenAI's o1 brought large benchmark gains that some count as a massive advance. 'All 7 held strong' is therefore only partly borne out. Whether it holds depends on reading 'modest profits' as a ceiling rather than a forecast of actual profit.
limitations: The seven predictions are taken from a secondary list, not from the post itself.
Several items (moat, adoption, number of models) have no agreed measure and were not tested.
Whether o1 counts as a 'massive advance' is subjective.
OpenAI's loss figure is a reported projection, not audited results.

public_payload.normalized_proposition: All seven of Marcus's March 2024 predictions that generative AI economics would be problematic have held.

statement.excerpt: All 7 of these economic predictions have held strong.

our_interpretation: The seven predictions are those in Marcus's March 2024 list for 'by end of 2024': 7-10 GPT-4 level models; no massive advance (no GPT-5, or disappointing GPT-5); price wars; very little moat for anyone; no robust solution to hallucinations; modest lasting corporate adoption; modest profits, split 7-10 ways.
The claim is checked as of the post date, December 11, 2024.

Plain reading of 'modest profits, split 7-10 ways': the leading model makers would earn some, but modest, profits. Large losses do not literally match this, though they fit his wider point that the economics were problematic.
The contract carries no single money metric because the claim bundles seven mostly non-financial predictions. The profit item is checked against reported OpenAI results.
criteria.support_condition: Evidence that each of the seven predictions matched the state of the field by December 11, 2024.
criteria.contradiction_condition: Credible evidence that one or more of the seven did not hold, for example no profits for the leading developer, or a clearly massive advance.

evidence.excerpt: I would say he's approximately correct regarding non-agent models, but o1 and o3 are big advances ("massive" is about right), and constitute more moat for OpenAI.
evidence.locator: section 'Predictions made in 2024', Gary Marcus entry
evidence.explanation: Lists the seven predictions: 7-10 GPT-4 level models, no massive advance, price wars, very little moat, no robust hallucination fix, modest adoption, and modest profits split 7-10 ways. The compiler judges them roughly correct but disputes the 'no massive advance' and 'moat' items. The publication date is approximate.

evidence.excerpt: Alibaba Cloud gave China’s AI industry a fresh shock on Tuesday after it announced a price cut of up to 97%
evidence.explanation: Steep 2024 price cuts by ByteDance, Alibaba and Baidu, described as an escalating price war. This supports the 'price wars' prediction.

evidence.excerpt: An open problem in artificial intelligence is how to train models that produce responses that are factually correct. Current language models sometimes produce false outputs or answers unsubstantiated by evidence, a problem known as “hallucinations”.
evidence.explanation: In late 2024 OpenAI itself called hallucinations an open problem and said GPT-4o scored under 40% on its new factuality benchmark. This supports 'no robust solution to hallucinations.'

evidence.excerpt: CNBC has confirmed that OpenAI expects about $5 billion in losses on $3.7 billion in revenue this year
evidence.explanation: The leading model maker expected a large 2024 loss, not 'modest profits.' Read literally, the profits prediction did not hold, though the result fits his wider warning about the economics.

evidence.excerpt: OpenAI o1 ranks in the 89th percentile on competitive programming questions (Codeforces), places among the top 500 students in the US in a qualifier for the USA Math Olympiad (AIME)
evidence.explanation: OpenAI reported large benchmark gains from o1 in September 2024. Some observers call this a massive advance, which challenges the 'no massive advance' prediction. Whether it counts is subjective.

public_payload.what_would_resolve: An agreed measure for the vague items, plus a ruling on whether large losses count as consistent with 'modest profits', would settle whether all seven held.
